![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14075717/assets/7cbcdf7d43a99b9558b1d085d2306c22e1d27134a5b0ea428721ce7bd074b725.png)

Consider the RCL circuit shown above. Given that the charge $q(t)$ of the capacitor at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
q(t)=A{e}^{-t}+B{e}^{-4t}+\frac{P}{17}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+\frac{Q}{17}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)
$$

where $A,$ $B,$ $P,$ and $Q$ are constants, find the value of $P+Q.$

*Hint: The voltage drop ${V}_{C}$ across the capacitor is related to its charge by $q=C{V}_{C},$ where $C$ is the capacitance measured in Farads.*
feedback.worked_solution:
The diagram shows a series RCL circuit with a source electromotive force (EMF) of $2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\,\text{V},$ a resistor of resistance $5\,Ω,$ a capacitor of capacitance $0.25\,\text{F},$ and an inductor of inductance $1\,\text{H}.$

The current $I,$ measured in amperes, is defined as the rate of flow of charge $q,$ measured in coulombs.

$$
I=\frac{dq}{dt}
$$

Kirchhoff's voltage law states that in a series circuit, the source voltage (EMF) equals the sum of the voltage drops.

In an RCL circuit, there are three voltage drops:

- The voltage drop across the resistor is proportional to the current, with a constant of proportionality $R=5\,Ω.$ So,

$$
{V}_{R}=5I=5\,\frac{dq}{dt}.
$$

- The voltage drop across the capacitor is related to its charge by $q=C{V}_{C}.$ Therefore,

$$
{V}_{C}=\frac{q}{C}=\frac{q}{0.25}=4q.
$$

- The voltage drop across the inductor is proportional to the rate of change of current, with a constant of proportionality $L=1\,\text{H}.$ Hence,

$$
{V}_{L}=1\,\frac{dI}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dq}{dt})=\frac{{d}^{2}q}{d{t}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, by Kirchhoff's voltage law, the differential equation governing the amount of charge $q$ on the capacitor is

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)=5\,\frac{dq}{dt}+4q+\frac{{d}^{2}q}{d{t}^{2}},
$$

which gives

$$
\frac{{d}^{2}q}{d{t}^{2}}+5\cdot \frac{dq}{dt}+4q=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t).
$$

The given equation is a second-order linear equation with constant coefficients. To find the general solution, we must sum the complementary and particular solutions.

- To find the complementary solution ${q}_{c},$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
\frac{{d}^{2}{q}_{c}}{d{t}^{2}}+5\cdot \frac{d{q}_{c}}{dt}+4{q}_{c}=0.
$$

Solving using an integration technique, such as a trial solution, we obtain the complementary solution

$$
{q}_{c}(t)=A{e}^{-t}+B{e}^{-4t},
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are constants.

- Next, we find the particular solution. Note that the right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is sinusoidal with argument $t.$ So, we assume that the particular solution is also a sinusoidal with argument $t,$ i.e.,

$$
{q}_{p}(t)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(t).
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{p} & =\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(t), \\ \frac{d{q}_{p}}{dt} & =-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(t), \\ \frac{{d}^{2}{q}_{p}}{d{t}^{2}} & =-\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(t),\end{aligned}
$$

into the inhomogeneous equation and group like terms on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,(-\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(t))+5(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(t))\,\,\, &  \\ +4(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(t)) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) \\ (3\alpha +5\beta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+(-5\alpha +3\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3\alpha +5\beta =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)) \\ -5\alpha +3\beta =2\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(t))\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-\frac{5}{17},$ $\beta =\frac{3}{17}.$ Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{q}_{p}(t)=-\frac{5}{17}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+\frac{3}{17}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t).
$$

Now, since the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary solution and the particular solution, the general solution in our case is

$$
q(t)={q}_{c}(t)+{q}_{p}(t)=A{e}^{-t}+B{e}^{-4t}-\frac{5}{17}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+\frac{3}{17}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t).
$$

Therefore, we have $P=-5,$ $Q=3,$ and

$$
P+Q=-5+3=-2.
$$
